text:
Trump with his USA hat(Image: Zuffa LLC)

Donald Trump was accused of dozing off during his 80th birthday UFC fight, where he had front row seats.

Partway through the event on the White House South Lawn, he was seen wearing a white baseball cap with USA emblazoned across the front. His less charitable critics suggested the hat was intended to cover his face while he slept.

Video footage from the event captured the US president, who celebrated his 80th birthday yesterday, seated beside UFC CEO Dana White. In the clip, Trump appears to have nodded off, leaning to one side with his eyes shut. Reacting to the video, one X user commented: "DID THEY PUT A HAT ON HIM TO HIDE HIS SHUT EYES?"

Another quipped: "That, and the breeze was wreaking havoc with his comb over."

Not letting it slide, a further user dubbed the hat a 'sleeping cap,' writing: "This sleeping cap is a perfect match for the 'Dozing Don' at his UFC event... he is currently the reigning champion of naptime among global political leaders."

A White House spokesman has consistently described the president's energy as "unmatched," and denied any suggestions he has been sleeping.

Footage appeared to show the president slumped to the side with his eyes closed(Image: X)

Trump's doctor claimed the president recorded a 30/30 score on a cognitive assessment test at his latest medical examination at the end of May, which the White House characterized as a "perfect bill of health."

Questions and allegations regarding Trump's mental and physical fitness have followed him since becoming the oldest person ever inaugurated as president in January last year. Another viewer remarked after watching the footage of Trump with his eyes apparently shut: "I mean, he's 80. 80! ! ! He needs to resign. He's too old, and he knows it."

The hat covered his face

The president reaching 80 has only intensified calls for a younger successor. Responding to a birthday greeting from the White House X account, one user demanded: "25th amendment now!".

Section four of the 25th Amendment deals with the issue of presidents who are "unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office," but don't acknowledge their incapacity. It would require the vice president and a majority of departmental heads to declare to the speaker of the House of Representatives and the Senate's second-highest ranking official of the president's inability to continue.

Trump had previously faced intense scrutiny for appearing to doze off during Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden the week prior, footage that Democrats quickly seized upon.

California congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez responded "WAKE TF UP" to that video, while the Lincoln Project described the Madison Square Garden appearance as "the most expensive taxpayer-funded nap".

The string of episodes had prompted detractors to use the "Commander-in-Sleep" moniker. Nevertheless, the White House has consistently dismissed suggestions that Trump falls asleep during public engagements.

Marco Rubio, addressing the question at a congressional hearing earlier this month, argued the reverse was true, that Trump worked "inhumane hours" and contacted his secretary of state during the early morning.
